heading_path: bb for scheduled Claude Code and Codex runs
text: A card on bb for a developer who wants Claude Code or Codex to run on a timer. Everything on this page is read, not run: the hub has not started a bb schedule. Read the stage table and the permission default first. Other places a schedule can live are compared in [Run it on a schedule with an approval step](../cheatsheets/schedule-with-approval.md).

title: bb for scheduled Claude Code and Codex runs
heading_path: bb for scheduled Claude Code and Codex runs
What it is
text: bb is a local server and app that runs Claude Code, Codex and other agent CLIs as threads ([bb]). Its builtin automations plugin fires an agent prompt or a stored script on a 5-field cron with a timezone, or once at a set time or delay ([bb]).

title: bb for scheduled Claude Code and Codex runs
heading_path: bb for scheduled Claude Code and Codex runs
What it can carry
text:
| Pipeline stage | bb feature |
|---|---|
| Fire on a timer | Automations: recurring cron or one-shot time or delay ([bb]) |
| Agent step | An agent automation that runs Claude Code or Codex ([bb]) |
| Script step (your render or upload script) | A stored script automation ([bb script runtime]) |
| Overlapping tick | "An automation has at most one active run." ([bb script runtime]) |
| Failed run | Retries after 30 seconds and then 60 seconds, never past the next scheduled run ([bb script runtime]) |
| Run history, pause, re-run | Run history and a sidebar to pause or re-run ([bb]) |
| Ask a person a question | Ask User Question card, open 30 minutes by default ([bb configuration]) |
| Generate video, images or audio | No bb feature |
| Approval gate before publish | No bb feature ([bb]) |
| Post to a platform | No bb feature |

"No bb feature" means none of the four bb records names one; the tool record lists orchestration as its only lever ([bb]). A failing run never pauses the automation ([bb script runtime]). A process that starts its own session, such as `tmux`, `setsid` or a daemon, is not stopped by bb ([bb script runtime]), so a long render launched that way is not cleaned up.

title: bb for scheduled Claude Code and Codex runs
heading_path: bb for scheduled Claude Code and Codex runs
How a schedule is declared
text:
The schedule flags, quoted from bb's automations skill ([bb], as quoted on 2026-11-12):

```text
--cron <expr>                  Recurring 5-field cron expression
--timezone <tz>                IANA timezone for --cron
--at <datetime>                One-shot run time, preferably ISO 8601
--in <duration>                One-shot delay, e.g. 30s, 5m, 2h, 1d
```

The full create command is not quoted in the record. Read `plugins/automations/skills/automations/references/creation.md`, the source named on the [bb] record.

title: bb for scheduled Claude Code and Codex runs
heading_path: bb for scheduled Claude Code and Codex runs
What must stay running
text: The bb server machine, awake. bb's guide says: "while the server machine is asleep or off, nothing can reach bb and running threads may stop" ([bb multiple devices]). The Keep Awake plugin runs caffeinate, but a closed laptop lid still sleeps ([bb]). All state, including automations, lives under `~/.bb/` by default ([bb configuration]).

title: bb for scheduled Claude Code and Codex runs
heading_path: bb for scheduled Claude Code and Codex runs
Permission modes for unattended runs
text:
The default when no mode is given, quoted ([bb]):

> When `--permission-mode` is omitted, the plugin chooses Approve for me (`auto`) when the provider supports it and otherwise uses Full Access (`full`).

In Full Access, the Claude Code provider setting `fullAccessApprovalsEnabled` defaults to false, and the docs say "`false` approves every request" ([bb configuration]). Set to true, it shows Claude Code's own `permissions.ask` rules, PreToolUse hooks that answer `ask`, and built-in safety checks ([bb configuration]). The records quote no other permission-mode values.

title: bb for scheduled Claude Code and Codex runs
heading_path: bb for scheduled Claude Code and Codex runs
Approval
text:
What exists:

- An agent can ask a person through the Ask User Question card, which stays open 30 minutes by default; a server restart closes every open question ([bb configuration]).
- A person can pause or re-run an automation from the sidebar ([bb]).

What does not:

- Automations have no approval step of their own ([bb]).
- The records do not say whether an automation run can raise an Ask User Question card.

A gate before publish has to come from elsewhere; options are in [Run it on a schedule with an approval step](../cheatsheets/schedule-with-approval.md).

heading_path: bb for scheduled Claude Code and Codex runs
Secrets and telemetry
text:
- Plugins are full-trust code inside the server process and keep secret settings under `<dataDir>/plugins/<id>/secrets/` ([bb configuration]).
- The script runtime injects `BB_SERVER_URL` and IDs, not secrets ([bb script runtime]).
- A code read recorded on the tool record shows variables passed with `--env-json` kept as a string map in the plugin's SQLite file, so API keys do not belong there; the docs do not say this ([bb]).
- Binding the server to 0.0.0.0 exposes an API that, in the docs' words, "is unauthenticated and permits command execution and file reads" ([bb configuration]). Keep it on 127.0.0.1 and use bb connect or Tailscale Serve for phone access ([bb configuration]).
- Telemetry, quoted: "Production runs (the desktop app, `npx bb-app`, and `pnpm start` checkouts) send anonymous usage telemetry" ([bb]). The record states that `BB_TELEMETRY=false` turns it off and that it goes to PostHog ([bb]). The saved quote stops before the opt-out sentence, so the opt-out is the record's paraphrase, not a verbatim quote.

- Missed-tick behaviour after sleep: not confirmed by the docs. The tool record's fit notes say a code read suggests missed ticks collapse into one run, and that no doc states it ([bb]).

title: First render in a day with Claude Code
heading_path: First render in a day with Claude Code
Procedure
text:
1. **Choose the stack on licence and side effects.**
   - [Remotion](../../catalog/tool/remotion-dev__remotion.md) is free for "a for-profit organization with up to 3 employees"; its notes say a bigger company needs a paid Company License. [Remotion 5.0](../../catalog/source/remotion.dev__docs__5-0-migration.md) makes company licence holders enable telemetry.
   - [HyperFrames](../../catalog/tool/heygen-com__hyperframes.md) has no licence fee per its notes; the hub's collected licence is Apache-2.0. Its [skill](../../catalog/source/github.com__heygen-com__hyperframes__blob__main__skills__hyperframes__skill.md.md) asks the agent to run a usage beacon at start.
   - Run here once: the HyperFrames CLI wrote outside the project, under the home directory: a config file with telemetry enabled and an anonymous id, a 199M cache with its own headless browser, and preview logs.
   - Run here once: the Remotion folder reached 857M, of which a downloaded browser in `node_modules/.remotion/` was 459M; `npx` also cached packages in `~/.npm/_npx` ([run log](../../examples/hyperframes-vs-remotion/results/remotion-runlog.md)).
2. **Install, knowing each vendor's documented command behaved differently.** Run here once:
   - HyperFrames: `npx hyperframes skills update` starts a skills installer with `--global` that writes into the home directory's agent skill folders. The agent did not run it and used the skills bundled in the local npm package (`node_modules/hyperframes/dist/skills/`). It scaffolded with `npx hyperframes init video --skip-skills --skill=hyperframes` and set `HYPERFRAMES_NO_TELEMETRY=1` and `DO_NOT_TRACK=1`; four help calls ran before the opt-out ([run log](../../examples/hyperframes-vs-remotion/results/hyperframes-runlog.md)).
   - Remotion: `npx remotion skill` does not exist in 4.0.543. The command is `npx remotion skills add`, which installed at project scope into `.agents/skills/` with symlinks in `.claude/skills/` ([run log](../../examples/hyperframes-vs-remotion/results/remotion-runlog.md)).
3. **Write a brief with exact copy, sizes and palette.** Copy the shape of [BRIEF.md](../../examples/hyperframes-vs-remotion/BRIEF.md): a table of on-screen copy per time slot, 1920 x 1080, 30 fps, 20.0 s (600 frames), H.264, background `#0F1419`, text `#F2F4F7`, one accent `#4CC38A`, system fonts only. Run here once, the brief was ambiguous on whether "Step 1" is on-screen copy; each arm read it differently and each lost a point for copy. State in your brief which labels appear on screen.
4. **Have the agent render stills before the full render.**
   - Remotion, from the [Remotion](../../catalog/tool/remotion-dev__remotion.md) record's notes: `npx remotion still <entry> <id> out.png --frame=N` for one PNG, and `npx remotion render <id> out/frames --frames=0,30,90 --image-format=png` for several (v4.0.502+).
   - HyperFrames: run here once, the agent used `npx hyperframes snapshot --review --json` before its render ([run log](../../examples/hyperframes-vs-remotion/results/hyperframes-runlog.md)). No HyperFrames record quotes a still command.
   - Run here once, both agents found their layout bugs only by rendering stills and looking.
   - For HyperFrames finals, the [issue 4435](../../catalog/source/github.com__heygen-com__hyperframes__issues__4435.md) record reports that with 4 parallel workers in screenshot mode the first frame of workers 1-3 came out fully transparent, intermittently; it quotes "`--workers 1` produces zero blank frames".
5. **Measure the file.** From the example:

   ```sh
   python3 examples/hyperframes-vs-remotion/measure.py hyperframes examples/hyperframes-vs-remotion/results/hyperframes.mp4 --out /tmp/hf.json
   ```

   [measure.py](../../examples/hyperframes-vs-remotion/measure.py) checks a readable MP4 at 1920x1080, 30 fps, 20.0 s +/- 0.5 s, h264, no black segment over 1.0 s after the first 0.5 s, and no frozen segment over 4.0 s. It does not check the 30 minute cap or the no-human-message rule. Its thresholds are constants for this brief; `--sheet out.png` adds a 12-frame contact sheet. Run here once, both files passed.
6. **Look for the defects the measurement cannot see.** See the next section.

title: First render in a day with Claude Code
heading_path: First render in a day with Claude Code
What each run got wrong
text:
All run here once, one run per stack, judged by one blind reviewer from stills ([review](../../examples/hyperframes-vs-remotion/results/review.md)). The reviewer scored HyperFrames 8 and Remotion 10 out of 12, and nobody watched either clip play.

| | HyperFrames | Remotion |
|---|---|---|
| Palette | added a grey quote panel and grey secondary text | default render decoded the accent as `#43B589`, not `#4CC38A`; the agent found `--color-space=bt709` in the CLI help, not in the skills |
| Transitions | three scene changes pass through a frame showing only the accent bar | two dissolves stack the outgoing and incoming headline for about five frames |
| Content | counts up to 147, so it shows 54 and 112, which are not in the brief | - |
| Found from stills | a data line readable for about 1.3 s, labels too small at phone width | an accent bar shrunk to nothing, non-opaque pixels during slides |

title: What each platform requires for automated, AI-assisted posts from one developer's own account
heading_path: What each platform requires for automated, AI-assisted posts from one developer's own account
text:
A table of platform rules for a developer who posts their own clips through official APIs. All of it is read, not run: the hub has posted nothing. Read the table, then the TikTok and YouTube sections. Every cell is from the record linked in its row unless the cell links another, as quoted on 2026-11-12; "not stated" means not stated in the record. Policy pages change without notice.

| Platform | Public posting without audit or review? | Daily or rate limit | AI disclosure rule | Monetisation rule on AI or mass-produced content | Price of posting |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| YouTube ([YT revisions], [YT insert]) | Yes since 2026-11-02; default privacy is public | "100 videos.insert calls" per day per project | Disclose realistic AI content ([YT disclosure]); API flag `status.containsSyntheticMedia` | Not "mass-produced, generic, repetitive, or manipulative" ([YT monetisation]) | No cost stated |
| TikTok ([TT guidelines], [TT direct post]) | No: unaudited posts are private-only | "typically around 15 posts per day/ creator account"; init 6 requests per minute per token | Label realistic AI content ([TT community]); API flag `is_aigc` | Not stated | Not stated |
| Instagram ([IG publishing]) | Not stated; app review for Advanced Access not read | "100 API-published posts within a 24-hour moving period" | `is_ai_generated` on the media container | Not stated | Not stated |
| Facebook Reels ([FB reels]) | Not stated; posts to a Page, not a profile | "30 API-published posts within a 24-hour moving period" | `is_ai_generated`, defaults to false | Primarily unoriginal accounts "may see their account deemed non-recommendable and demonetized" ([Meta originality]) | Not stated |
| Threads ([Threads posts]) | Not stated; app review not read | "250 published posts within a 24-hour period" | `is_made_with_ai`; false "does not prevent automatic AI labeling" | Not stated | Not stated |
| X ([X pricing], [X automation]) | Not stated; automated posts allowed "for entertainment, informational, or novelty purposes" | Not stated | No label required or offered ([X authenticity]) | No monetisation rule; "duplicative or substantially similar posts" banned | "$0.015 per request", "$0.200" with a URL |
| LinkedIn ([LinkedIn share]) | Own profile: add the self-serve Share on LinkedIn product | No daily limit found | Not stated | Not stated | Not stated |
| Bluesky ([Bluesky video]) | No audit mentioned; verified email needed | A daily video-post limit exists; number not on the page | Not stated | Not stated | Not stated |
| Mastodon ([Mastodon posting]) | No app review; own-account token | Rate limits not read | Not stated | Not stated | Not stated |

title: What each platform requires for automated, AI-assisted posts from one developer's own account
heading_path: What each platform requires for automated, AI-assisted posts from one developer's own account
The TikTok dead end
text: TikTok's guidelines say: "all content uploaded via this endpoint will be restricted to private viewing mode. To lift this restriction, your API client must undergo an audit" ([TT guidelines]). The audit's intended-use list then rejects the one-developer case: "Not acceptable: A utility tool to help upload contents to the account(s) you or your team manages." ([TT guidelines]). An unaudited client is also blocked unless the account itself is private ([TT direct post]). Posts can be made public later by hand in the app ([TT guidelines]).

title: What each platform requires for automated, AI-assisted posts from one developer's own account
heading_path: What each platform requires for automated, AI-assisted posts from one developer's own account
What changed on YouTube on 2026-11-02
text: The revision history says: "Videos uploaded through the videos.insert method from unverified API projects are no longer restricted to private viewing mode." ([YT revisions]). It adds: "If you don't specify a value for the status.privacyStatus property in a videos.insert request, the uploaded video's privacy status defaults to public." ([YT revisions]). A test upload therefore needs `status.privacyStatus` set explicitly.

title: What each platform requires for automated, AI-assisted posts from one developer's own account
heading_path: What each platform requires for automated, AI-assisted posts from one developer's own account
Contradictions inside a platform's docs
text:
- Instagram: the guide quotes 100 API posts per 24 hours in its rate-limit section, and the record notes 50 published posts per 24 hours in the carousel section; the record advises planning for 50 ([IG publishing]).
- LinkedIn: the Videos API gives "Between 75kb and 500MB", and the record notes the same page also states 5 GB ([LinkedIn share]).
- YouTube: the July 28, 2020 private-only rule is still on the same revision page; the 2026-11-02 entry reverses it ([YT revisions]).

title: What each platform requires for automated, AI-assisted posts from one developer's own account
heading_path: What each platform requires for automated, AI-assisted posts from one developer's own account
C2PA and labels
text: A C2PA manifest is "digitally signed by a trusted implementation" ([C2PA]). YouTube says content "containing C2PA metadata" gets a label the creator "can not" adjust ([YT disclosure]). YouTube is the only platform record found that states it reads C2PA ([C2PA]). On Threads, leaving `is_made_with_ai` false does not prevent automatic AI labelling ([Threads posts]).

title: What each platform requires for automated, AI-assisted posts from one developer's own account
heading_path: What each platform requires for automated, AI-assisted posts from one developer's own account
Self-hosted schedulers and their limits
text:

title: Run it on a schedule with an approval step
heading_path: Run it on a schedule with an approval step
A pipeline with a gate before publish
text:
1. The schedule fires: [bb], [Hermes Agent], [cloud tasks][CC routines] or the [GitHub Actions schedule].
2. The agent writes and renders the clip: [claude -p] or [codex exec]. The renderer is your choice; the [worked example](../../examples/hyperframes-vs-remotion/README.md) was run here once.
3. Measure the file. Your own script; the example's `measure.py` is one model of it.
4. Stop for a person: required reviewers ([GitHub environments]), [n8n], [Windmill], [Trigger.dev] waitpoints, or a paused [Hermes Agent] job.
5. Publish with the platform's official API. Your own script; platform rules are in [publishing rules](publishing-rules.md).
6. Log what was posted. Your own script.

On GitHub, an environment secret stays locked until a required reviewer approves the job ([GitHub environments]), so the publish key can sit behind step 4.

title: Fact-check results
heading_path: Fact-check results
text:
What this is: the measured error rate of the hub's records, for anyone deciding how much to
rely on them. Read the summary, then the table, then the caveats.

All numbers on this page come from [evals/factcheck/2026-11-12.json](../evals/factcheck/2026-11-12.json).

title: Fact-check results
heading_path: Fact-check results
Summary
text:
On 2026-11-12 a different agent tool from the ones that wrote the records compared
112 records with the saved copies of their sources.

- **Quotes: 296 of 296 are verbatim.**
- **Claims: 39 of 296 (13.2%) said more than the source.**
  38 were overstated: a dropped condition, a wider scope. 1 was wrong.
- **Prose** (summaries and fit notes): 1504 statements. 74 overstated,
  22 not in the saved source, 4 wrong. 311 could not be
  checked from the saved source and are not counted as errors.
- **Category fields: 17 of 216 were not backed by the saved source.**

No invented quote and no wrong number was found in a quote. The typical fault is a true
sentence with its limiting clause removed.

title: Fact-check results
heading_path: Fact-check results
Method
text:
- Checker: codex CLI. Writers: kiro CLI for most lanes, the driver agent for the first seven
  records. The checker got each record and the saved copy of its source, not the writer's notes.
- Unit: the atomic claim. Each got one verdict: supported, overstated, wrong, outdated, or
  not in source. Each quote was checked for being verbatim.
- First a seeded random sample: seed 20261112, 6 records per lane, 70 records,
  181 claims. Sample rate: 13.3%.
- Then every remaining record of the four lanes whose sample rate was over 15%.
- The checker did not open live pages. It judged each record against its own source.

- [OpenMontage](../../catalog/tool/openmontageinc__openmontage.md) lists TikTok dead zones on 1080x1920 of 108 px top, 320 px bottom, 120 px right; its record says the table cites a third-party site that was not opened.
- [remotion-superpowers](../../catalog/tool/dojocodinglabs__remotion-superpowers.md): "About 15-25% up from the bottom (`bottom` around 300-480), or dead center for punchy hooks".
- [Remotion Agent Skills](../../catalog/tool/remotion-dev__skills.md), for 1080px-wide video: "keep key text at least 80px from the sides and 100px from the top and bottom."

Standard: [Meta's Reels ads guide](../../catalog/source/facebook.com__business__ads-guide__update__video__instagram-reels.md) says "Consider leaving at least 14% of the top, 35% of the bottom, and 6% on each side of your asset free from text". It is written for ads; [TikTok's ads page](../../catalog/source/ads.tiktok.com__help__article__creative-best-practices.md) gives safe zones only as files that were not downloaded. What to do: for Reels, keep captions outside Meta's margins; for TikTok the hub has no first-party number.

title: Where the skills contradict each other, and what the standards say
heading_path: Where the skills contradict each other, and what the standards say
Loudness target
text:
- [motion-graphics (Mort1d)](../../catalog/tool/mort1d__motion-graphics-skills.md) masters at "-14 LUFS, true peak ≤ -1 dBTP".
- [SynthCut](../../catalog/tool/relo-video__synthcut.md) ships "platform export presets with loudness normalization (-14/-16 LUFS)".
- [generative-media-skills](../../catalog/tool/calesthio__generative-media-skills.md): "Leave at least 1 dB true-peak headroom for generic web/social delivery when no loudness target is specified".

Standard: [EBU R 128](../../catalog/source/tech.ebu.ch__publications__r128.md) sets "a Target Level of −23.0 LUFS" and a true peak that "shall not exceed −1 dBTP". [EBU R 128 s2](../../catalog/source/tech.ebu.ch__files__live__sites__tech__files__shared__r__r128s2.pdf.md) allows "the range of −20.0 to −16.0 LUFS" for streaming without metadata, and its record marks the -14 LUFS skill as above that range. What to do: the s2 record's notes say pick -16 LUFS integrated with -1 dBTP and check with `ffmpeg -i out.mp4 -af ebur128=peak=true -f null -` (from the R 128 record).

title: Where the skills contradict each other, and what the standards say
heading_path: Where the skills contradict each other, and what the standards say
Frames or numbers in review
text:
- [remotion-superpowers](../../catalog/tool/dojocodinglabs__remotion-superpowers.md): "if they disagree on something visible, trust the frames and say so."
- [screenstudio-alt](../../catalog/tool/connerkward__screenstudio-alternative-skill.md): "send the actual rendered mp4 to a video-understanding model and act on its critique."
- [smooth-animation-skill](../../catalog/tool/flchntc__smooth-animation-skill.md) fails a file on a number: "the limit is 0.1."

No standard decides it. [arXiv 2605.15585](../../catalog/source/arxiv.org__abs__2605.15585.md) says such defects "become apparent only after execution". In the [worked example](../../examples/hyperframes-vs-remotion/README.md), run here once, both agents found their layout bugs only from stills. What to do: [ffmpeg-skill](../../catalog/tool/kajisho5__ffmpeg-skill.md) runs both, a `check.py` step and then a `look.py` contact sheet.

title: Where the skills contradict each other, and what the standards say
heading_path: Where the skills contradict each other, and what the standards say
Motion timing
text:
- [HyperFrames](../../catalog/tool/heygen-com__hyperframes.md): "**Exits** are 40-50% shorter than their entrances."
- [motion-design skill](../../catalog/tool/lottiefiles__motion-design-skill.md): "Stagger total <500ms". [claude-remotion-skill](../../catalog/tool/haidrrrry__claude-remotion-skill.md): "**NEVER use linear interpolation.**"
- [Carbon](../../catalog/source/carbondesignsystem.com__elements__motion__overview.md): "the larger the change in distance (traveled) or size (scaling) of the element, the longer the animation takes." Its record says Carbon's exit easing speeds up, matching HyperFrames.
- [Material 3 tokens](../../catalog/source/github.com__material-components__material-web__blob__main__tokens__versions__latest__sass___md-sys-motion.scss.md): medium durations of 250, 300, 350 and 400 ms; its record says these are for taps.

No design-system record gives an exit-to-entrance ratio, so no standard decides it. What to do: the Carbon record's notes say scale UI durations up for video and keep the ratios.

text:
- [Remotion](../../catalog/tool/remotion-dev__remotion.md) LICENSE: free for "a for-profit organization with up to 3 employees".

title: An agent fixes a clip from checker output alone
heading_path: An agent fixes a clip from checker output alone
text:
What this is: one experiment with [clipcheck](../../lab/clipcheck/README.md), the hub's contract
checker. For anyone building a review loop for agent-made video. Read the result table, then
"What the checker got wrong".

**Status: ran.** One clip, one agent run, one reviewer, on 2026-11-12. A tiny sample. It shows
the loop works once and where it misleads. It does not show how often.

title: An agent fixes a clip from checker output alone
heading_path: An agent fixes a clip from checker output alone
Goal
text:
Every skill in the hub tells the agent to render stills and look at them. Can a deterministic
checker carry the review loop instead: seconds per run, frame-exact, no vision tokens? And if
an agent optimises against a checker, does the clip get better or does it only pass?

title: An agent fixes a clip from checker output alone
heading_path: An agent fixes a clip from checker output alone
Setup
text:
- The clip: the HyperFrames arm of [the first example](../hyperframes-vs-remotion/README.md),
  which a blind reviewer had marked down for frames that showed only an accent bar and for a
  counter that ran through numbers the brief does not contain.
- The contract: [quote-first.json](../../lab/clipcheck/contracts/quote-first.json). It is the
  example's brief as data: size, palette, safe area, scene times, copy, allowed numbers.
- The agent: a fresh Claude subagent given the project and the checker. Its only feedback was
  the checker's output. It was told not to render stills, open images or run any review command.
- Stop rule: `CLIPCHECK: PASS`, or 4 fix rounds, or 30 minutes.
- Then a blind review: a separate agent scored the before and after clips as "B" and "A" on a
  six-point rubric, from a brief with the tool names removed. It was asked to list differences
  that made a clip worse as well as better.

title: An agent fixes a clip from checker output alone
heading_path: An agent fixes a clip from checker output alone
Threshold (fixed before the run)
text:
The experiment passes if the agent reaches `CLIPCHECK: PASS` inside the stop rule **and** the
blind reviewer does not score the after clip lower than the before clip. A pass on the checker
with a lower reviewer score would be published as a negative result.

title: An agent fixes a clip from checker output alone
heading_path: An agent fixes a clip from checker output alone
Results
text:
Checker verdicts, measured here by `clipcheck.py` with the rules as committed
([before](results/clipcheck-before.json), [after](results/clipcheck-after.json)):

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Verdict | fail | pass |
| Errors | 1 | 0 |
| Warnings | 1 | 0 |
| Findings | empty-frames at 2.967-3.167 s, 7.967-8 s, 13-13.033 s; stray-numbers (126) at 14 s | none |

From the agent's log ([agent-runlog.md](results/agent-runlog.md)), self-reported:

| | |
|---|---|
| Fix rounds to pass | 2 |
| Renders | 3, about 11 s each |
| Wall time | about 3.5 minutes |
| Frames looked at | none |

Blind review, one reviewer, judgement ([review.md](results/review.md)):

| Criterion (0-2) | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Copy exact | 1 | 1 |
| Hierarchy and type | 2 | 2 |
| Alignment and safe area | 1 | 1 |
| Palette obeyed | 1 | 1 |
| Entrances and transitions | 1 | 2 |
| Nothing clipped, overlapping or broken | 0 | 1 |
| Total out of 12 | 6 | 8 |

The reviewer compared the clips frame by frame and listed seven differences. It judged the
after clip better at four of them, marginally better at one, saw no visible difference at one,
and gave no verdict at one.

Clips: [before.mp4](results/before.mp4), [after.mp4](results/after.mp4). Contact sheets:
[before](results/before-sheet.png), [after](results/after-sheet.png). The agent's edited
scenes: [results/source-after/](results/source-after/).

Verdict against the threshold: **pass**.

title: An agent fixes a clip from checker output alone
heading_path: An agent fixes a clip from checker output alone
What the agent changed
text:
- **Empty frames at three scene changes.** Cause: two exit tweens ended one frame before the
  cut, and two scenes entered from zero opacity. Fix: later exit starts, and entrances that
  begin at 25 to 30 percent opacity.
- **A counter running from 0 to 147.** Fix: the count-up was removed; 147 is revealed as static
  text. The reviewer counted 17 intermediate values in the before clip. The checker had read
  only one of them (126), because it reads on-screen text every 0.5 s.
- **A scene change with nothing moving**, which the first fix had introduced. Fix: the next
  scene's entrance starts at the cut.

title: An agent fixes a clip from checker output alone
heading_path: An agent fixes a clip from checker output alone
What the checker got wrong
text:
- **It pushed the agent to change something that was fine.** The first version of the
  "long hold" rule ignored slow motion, so three line wipes read as a 4.4 s hold. To clear the
  warning the agent shortened the wipes from 12 frames to 4. The reviewer gave no verdict on
  that change and noted that a 2-frame reveal "may be too fast to register as motion". The rule
  has since been corrected; with the committed rules the before clip no longer raises it. This
  is the main lesson of the run: an agent optimises against the checker, including its mistakes.
- **It cannot tell readable from present.** After the fix, incoming headlines are on screen at
  the cut but blurred and dim. The checker counts the frame as not empty. The reviewer called
  one of them "an unreadable ghost headline for 2 frames".
- **It missed defects the reviewer found in both clips**: text sliding across the accent bar at
  12.8 s, a grey panel behind the quote, "Step N" labels that the brief does not list as copy,
  and a layout that leaves the right half of the frame empty.

title: An agent fixes a clip from checker output alone
heading_path: An agent fixes a clip from checker output alone
Limits
text:
- One clip, one agent run, one reviewer.
- The agent ran against an earlier version of the checker, which also raised the false "long
  hold" warning. The table above is measured with the corrected rules.
- The agent read two threshold constants in the checker's source when the output did not
  explain a finding. That is more than "output only". The messages now state those thresholds.
- The same reviewer protocol scored this "before" clip 8 of 12 in the first example and 6 of 12
  here. Scores from different review sessions are not comparable; only the two columns of one
  session are.
- Motion was judged from stills. Nobody watched either clip play.
- Not measured: token cost of either review style, repeatability, other renderers.

heading_path: An agent fixes a clip from checker output alone

text:

python3 lab/clipcheck/clipcheck.py examples/clipcheck-fix-loop/results/before.mp4 --contract lab/clipcheck/contracts/quote-first.json
python3 examples/clipcheck-fix-loop/test_smoke.py
```

heading_path: Same brief, HyperFrames vs Remotion, vendor skills only
Goal
text:
With only the vendor's own skills and one fixed [brief](BRIEF.md), does a Claude agent get a
spec-conformant 20 s clip out of each stack, locally, with no human help? What defects does
each first deliverable carry?

title: Same brief, HyperFrames vs Remotion, vendor skills only
heading_path: Same brief, HyperFrames vs Remotion, vendor skills only
Setup
text:
- Agent under test: one fresh Claude subagent per arm, given the brief and an empty folder.
- Skills: the ones each vendor ships. No other skills, no web search, no example repos.
- Machine: Apple M3 Max, 64 GB, macOS, Node 22, ffmpeg 7.1.1. Local render only.
- No human message during a run. A 30 minute cap.
- The pass or fail thresholds below were written down before either arm ran.

title: Same brief, HyperFrames vs Remotion, vendor skills only
heading_path: Same brief, HyperFrames vs Remotion, vendor skills only
Threshold (fixed before the run)
text:
An arm passes when its file is a readable MP4 at 1920x1080, 30 fps, 20.0 s +/- 0.5 s, h264,
has no black segment over 1.0 s after the first 0.5 s, no frozen segment over 4.0 s, and was
delivered inside the cap with no human message. [measure.py](measure.py) checks all but the
last two.

Results
Blind review (judgement, one reviewer, one clip per arm)
text:
A separate agent scored the two clips as "A" and "B" on six criteria, 0 to 2 each, from
stills. Full text with frame evidence: [results/review.md](results/review.md).

| Criterion | HyperFrames | Remotion |
|---|---|---|
| Copy exact | 1 | 1 |
| Hierarchy and type | 2 | 2 |
| Alignment and safe area | 2 | 2 |
| Palette obeyed | 1 | 2 |
| Entrances and transitions | 1 | 2 |
| Nothing clipped, overlapping or broken | 1 | 1 |
| Total out of 12 | 8 | 10 |

Why the two points differ, in the reviewer's words: the HyperFrames clip added a grey quote
panel and grey secondary text to the three briefed colours, and three of its scene changes
pass through a frame that shows only the accent bar. The Remotion clip's two dissolves stack
the outgoing and incoming headline for about five frames.

The reviewer could not judge easing or how the motion feels at speed. Nobody watched either
clip play.

title: Same brief, HyperFrames vs Remotion, vendor skills only
heading_path: Same brief, HyperFrames vs Remotion, vendor skills only
What the runs found
text:
These are single observations from one run each.

- **Both install commands differ from the documentation.**
  - HyperFrames: `npx hyperframes skills update` starts a skills installer with `--global`
    that writes into the home directory's agent skill folders. The agent read that in the CLI
    source and did not run it. It used the skills bundled in the local npm package instead.
  - Remotion: `npx remotion skill` does not exist in 4.0.543. The command is
    `npx remotion skills add`, and it installs at project scope.
- **The HyperFrames CLI wrote outside the project**: a config file with telemetry enabled and
  an anonymous id, a 199M cache with its own headless browser, and preview logs, all under
  the home directory. The agent set `HYPERFRAMES_NO_TELEMETRY=1` and `DO_NOT_TRACK=1` and
  skipped the usage beacons the skill asks for. Four help calls ran before the opt-out.
- **Remotion's default render was untagged for colour.** The first render decoded the accent
  as `#43B589` instead of the briefed `#4CC38A`. The agent found `--color-space=bt709` in the
  CLI help and used it for the final. That flag is not in the skills. The skills-only render
  is described in the run log.
- **Both agents found their layout bugs only by rendering stills and looking.** HyperFrames:
  a data line readable for about 1.3 s, labels too small at phone width. Remotion: an accent
  bar that had shrunk to nothing, and non-opaque pixels during slides.
- **Each skill shaped the result in a visible way.** HyperFrames' motion rules produced four
  different entrances and three kinds of seam. Remotion's `TransitionSeries` rule produced
  overlapping transitions with no empty frame at a cut.
- **The HyperFrames clip counts up to 147**, so it shows numbers that are not in the brief
  (54, 112) on the way. For a line that reports a verification result, that is a defect.

title: Same brief, HyperFrames vs Remotion, vendor skills only
heading_path: Same brief, HyperFrames vs Remotion, vendor skills only
Limits
text:
- One run per arm. A second run could reverse any difference here.
- The agent under test was a Claude subagent, not an interactive Claude Code session, and
  it could not open a live preview.
- The HyperFrames arm used the skills bundled in the npm package, not the ones the installer
  fetches. They were not compared.
- The reviewer's brief names both toolchains, so it knew which two stacks were compared,
  though not which clip was which.
- The brief is ambiguous on whether "Step 1" is on-screen copy. Each arm read it differently
  and each lost a point for copy.
- Wall time, render counts and fix counts come from the agents' logs.
- Not measured: token cost, repeatability, audio, motion at playback speed.

heading_path: Same brief, HyperFrames vs Remotion, vendor skills only

python3 examples/hyperframes-vs-remotion/test_smoke.py
```

Setup

What the skill bought
text:
- **Exact copy.** The contract's `copy` list and `decisions` settled the questions that cost
  both agents a point in the first example: no role labels, no added quote marks, no
  count-up. The reviewer found "all ten strings present as written".
- **No broken frames.** The skill's cause-level rules ("the exit ends at the cut", "reveal, do
  not count up") gave a clip that passed every frame rule on its first render, with no fix
  round.
- **Palette discipline.** No panel fill, no extra grey.
- **A second pair of eyes that found things.** The clean-context reviewer caught a heading at
  a different height in each scene, a rule missing on the cut frame, and scenes that sat on a
  heading alone. The checker cannot measure any of them.

heading_path: Does the hub's own skill change the result?
What the skill cost
text:
- **Transitions became cuts.** The skill says an incoming element must be readable when it
  arrives and must not fade in from a blur. The agent followed it literally: every scene
  change is "a 4-frame blur/fade/rise of the old scene", then "the new headline is on screen
  at full opacity on the very next frame". The reviewer scored this below the vendor-only
  clip's three designed transitions. The checker passed it, because its scene-change rule only
  asks for motion at the cut.
- **A flatter design.** The reviewer found headline and supporting text "close in size", small
  green text of about 30 px, and "same layout and same transition four times". The vendor-only
  clip was "the more designed and varied piece".
- **More time.** 9.9 minutes and 3 renders against 7 minutes 46 seconds and 1.

The pattern: a skill made of prohibitions removes defects and removes ambition with them. The
rule that prevented an unreadable frame also prevented a transition.

Limits
text:
- One run per arm, one reviewer. The reviewer called one of its own scores "borderline".
- **The skill was written after seeing the vendor-only clip's defects.** It is tuned to this
  brief. A brief it has never seen is the fair test and has not been run.
- The arms are not matched: the vendor-only run happened earlier, with a 30 minute cap and the
  vendor's own review commands; the with-skill run had a 40 minute cap.
- This reviewer scored the vendor-only clip 9 of 12. Earlier sessions scored the same file 8
  and 6. Only the two columns of one session compare.
- Motion was judged from stills. Nobody watched either clip play.
- The skill has been edited since this run (see below). The edited version is untested.
